jobs.prompt:
Third Opus review of the auto-approve policy: FAIL (3 high). Fix all, one test each in tests/auto-approve.test.mjs, keep all other guard, approval and swarm-merge tests passing; keep removing capability rather than parsing it.
H1 URL normaliser: the scp-like pattern accepts transport-helper URLs (a helper on PATH runs the push). Reject any URL containing a double colon anywhere and require the user part to match only letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen; ssh and https schemes only.
H2 the checks use hardened config (global and system blanked, hooks, fsmonitor and credentials overridden) but the approved command itself runs with the real global and XDG gitconfig (insteadOf, sshCommand, global hooksPath, credential helpers) and inherited git environment variables that an earlier command could have exported. Fix: the hook runs checks AND records the exact argv; at execution the command must run in the same hardened environment: have the policy rewrite approved git commands so the guard only allows them when the session environment has no git environment variable set (check process env) and, in addition, verify the effective config from every scope (git config --show-origin --list under the real environment) against the same allow-list, refusing disallowed keys including those from the global and XDG files; block session writes to the gitconfig files in the home directory and the XDG git config folder.
H3 unparseable (opaque) commands: an opaque command is pushed as a commit op and can be covered by a policy window, but policyGitInvocationsFromOps drops opaque ops so the guard returns allow with no kill switch, shell check or rate limits. Never let a policy row cover an opaque or non-git op; deny in applyPolicyGuardedAllow whenever any op is opaque.
M1 deleting stats.json still resets counters: once the initialised marker exists, a missing stats file is treated as unreadable (limit reached); confirm Bash rm and mv outside orchestrator mode under the handbuild state folder are denied and add the test.
M2 the config checks fail open when git config --local --list errors (gitRepoLocalConfigSafe returns true, gitOriginUrlRewritesPresent fails open): return unsafe on any error.
M3 any binary named git is accepted (basename test): require the executable word to be exactly git, resolved from a trusted PATH.
M4 commit -F reads the message from any file: drop -F (only -m).
M5 git add does not check paths: require every pathspec to be a literal path covered by the window and refuse a leading colon (magic pathspec).
M6 symlinked prefix for new files: deepestExistingRel accepts any existing prefix: require the resolved prefix to equal the raw prefix.
M7 the standing merge allow skips the policy guard for the whole command: skip only when the merge is the only op.
L1 worktreeIsClean and gitWorktreePolicyContext call git without the hardened environment: use the hardened runner. L2 pick the window that covers the op, deny when ambiguous. L3 drop --author on commits. L4 apply the code-extension filter to docs plans, docs state and docs scope too. L5 the policy file override marker is a constant string and the standing-merge path skips it: drop the environment override entirely. L6 anchor the SAFE_SWARM pattern at the command start in tools/self-approval.mjs.
